description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/memory.rs:193-235 implements MemoryBackend::demo_next_id with a two-mode helper (deterministic len()-based default, or realistic-demo-ids feature for a process-global timestamp+counter). The canonical mail-server (crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:961-979) does NOT use demo_next_id; it uses uuid::Uuid::new_v4() directly inside create_object. The canonical's pattern is collision-free and persistent-across-restarts ish; the sharing sibling's default mode has documented collision-on-delete (per the inline comment at memory.rs:215-220 and the workspace-tracked bead bd:JMAP-qz9v.14).

Per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates': if a sibling reshapes its impl in a way that diverges from the canonical, the canonical changes first then the sibling propagates. The reverse is a regression of cookie-cutter intent.

The 920fb0d commit landed demo_next_id in 6 siblings (chat, calendars, contacts, metadata, sharing, tasks) but explicitly excluded mail-server. The commit message acknowledges the workspace-wide drift as a deliberate mitigation against cargo-culting the worse mail-server pattern — but that reverses the canonical-template precedence rule.

Two resolutions:
  (a) Propagate demo_next_id to mail-server's create_object as the new canonical (drop uuid::Uuid::new_v4()).
  (b) Revert the 6 siblings to use uuid::Uuid::new_v4() matching the canonical (then revisit the cargo-cult concern that motivated 920fb0d).

Neither is a one-line fix. This is the meta-finding the cookie-cutter rule says review should catch. Cross-references: bd:JMAP-qz9v.14, bd:JMAP-826m.18, bd:JMAP-qz9v.47, bd:JMAP-qz9v.46, bd:JMAP-ayoz.20, bd:JMAP-x2gd.63.
title: MemoryBackend::demo_next_id diverges from canonical mail-server's uuid-based create_object
